title: Credit and Financial Services: Rural Financial Services Programme
description: The programme is aimed at creating a healthy and extensive rural finance system that would, consequently, offer rural population and households the opportunity for higher and more stable income, thus alleviating poverty.  More specifically, the programme would: (a) fill existing gaps in the support currently available to the microfinance subsector in order to enhance the quality of rural financial services and render them viable, with high quality of portfolio; (b) facilitate the expansion of sustainable financial services to substantially reach more of the country''s rural population than hitherto; (c) extend financial services to areas that have heretofore been poorly served; and (d) help potential clientele of rural MFIs to become more and increasingly business-oriented.

title: Rural Development: District Livelihoods Support Programme
description: Key Project Objectives: The goal of the Programme is to achieve significant improvement in the standard and sustainability of livelihoods of poor rural households. Supporting objectives are: rural communities are empowered and self-reliant; household productivity and incomes are sustainably increased; individual and communal land is better managed and rationally utilised; critical infrastructure and services are accessible; and Districts are supported to provide services locally.Policy and Institutional Objectives: The Programme supports the deepening of the decentralisation process and its implementation in newer districts. In order to address some of the specific constraints that poor people face with regard to land tenure, land management and women''s rights, the proposed Programme includes specific measures to support new land, land use and domestic relations policies at the District level.

title: Rural Development: Community Agricultural Infrastructure Improvement Programme
description: The overall programme goal is to contribute to poverty reduction and economic growth in Uganda through enhanced commercialisation of agriculture. The specific objectives of the Programme are to enhance farmers'' access to markets, improve prices and increased incomes through investments in rural infrastructures and their sustainable management by well mobilised communities.

title: Research/Extension/Training: Agricultural Technology and Agribusiness Advisory Services Programme
description: Key project objectivesThe development objective is to increase agricultural productivity and incomes of participating households by improving the performance of agricultural research and advisory services, while enhancing environmental sustainability and resilience to climate risks and land degradation.Policy and institutional objectivesNARO and NAADS recognise that a closer alliance between the two institutions together with effective partnerships with other stakeholders is crucial to achieving expected outcomes and impacts.  Closer links will be forged by developing strong NARO-NAADS research-advisory interfaces at the national, zonal and local levels.  Stakeholder platforms and public private partnerships will be promoted to develop pathways for the uptake of technology by farmers along priority value chains.

title: Agricultural Development: Vegetable Oil Development Project 2
description: The development objective is to increase the domestic production of vegetable oil and its by-products, thus raising rural incomes for smallholder producers and ensuring the supply of affordable vegetable oil products to Ugandan consumers. The project will achieve this by supporting farmers to increase their production of crushing material (both oil palm and oilseeds) and establishing commercial relations to directly link them to processors.The project will support the adoption of modern oilseed cropping techniques by farmers (with a focus on soybean) and will build direct relations between processors and farmer groups. For oil palm, KOPGT will become self-financing within five years and will become the institution for promoting smallholder oil palm development in Uganda.  OSSUP will continue to coordinate the sub-sector, and oil palm processors will be encouraged to join.

title: Credit and Financial Services: Rural Finance Programme
description: The programme''s development goal is to improve the livelihoods of rural households.  Central to achieving this goal and as its overall objective, the programme aims to increase the use of sustainable financial services in rural areas.  This will be achieved through investments in five components to:  (i) develop the use of sustainable community-based financial institutions; (ii) promote rural banking services; (iii) increase and intensify small-scale production in contract-farming operations; (iv) develop new and expanding existing financial service products in rural areas; and (v) establish a more conducive policy and institutional framework for rural finance.

title: Livestock: Smallholder Livestock Investment Project
description: The goal is to increase incomes and food security among poor smallholder farmers through restoration of access to draught animal power.  The project''s two objectives are:  (i) reduction in the incidence of Contagious Bovine Pleuro-pneumonia and East Coast Fever to levels that allow re-establishment and growth of smallholder cattle herds; and (ii) re-stocking of smallholder farmers, who have lost their cattle due to disease, to a level and in a manner which will provide them with sustainable access to draught animal power.

title: Marketing/Storage/Processing: Smallholder Agribusiness Promotion Programme
description: The overall goal is to increase the income levels of poor rural households involved in the production, value adding and trade of agricultural commodities. The programme aims to achieve this by increasing the volume and value of agribusiness based on the output of small-scale producers.SAPP will support the realignment of functions between the public and private sectors, completing the transition process that started in the 1990s.  In essence, GRZ will deliver public-good type services to agribusiness including, research and extension, the application of quality, health and safety regulations, development project management, and maintenance of an enabling commercial environment built around the common law of contract.  Interventionist activities such subsidised input and marketing operations, are being transferred to the private sector, outsourced or downsized.The Programme's institutional strategy is to work through, complement and strengthen the main actors at the various levels in selected value chains, including government agencies, cooperatives, NGOs, agribusiness enterprises, farmer organisations, and other programmes and projects.  In this way, the expected institutional outcomes of the Programme are:a) MACO, through the SAPPO and its contracted service providers, coordinating Programme initiatives and taking the lead in policy development in the areas of private sector partnership-building and value chain enhancement;b) MACO's ABM Department with the capacity to take full responsibility for the formulation and execution of key policy and regulatory functions and the creation of an enabling environment for rural commercial development which is inclusive of small-farmers;c) private sector partners willing to enter into mutually beneficial PPPs which deliver the desired outcomes in terms of agricultural commercialisation and rural poverty reduction, as well as profitable and sustainable agribusiness enterprises;d)Provinces and Districts with improved capacity to support agribusiness development which meet the specific needs small-scale farmers and other actors in the selected value chains;e)sustainable and self-financing farmer organisations, enterprise groups, trade associations, and commodity task forces providing support services fully engaged in the implementation of Programme activities, and policy/regulatory reform; andf)productive and mutually beneficial partnerships with a range of sub-sectoral institutions, service providers and industry organisations.

title: Research/Extension/Training: Smallholder Productivity Promotion Programme
description: Building on the experiences of the IFAD-funded Smallholder Agribusiness Promotion Programme (SAPP), the programme will sustainably increase smallholder production, productivity and sales of smallholder farmers in the targeted areas.  At the goal level, the Programme is expected to assist up to 48,000 smallholder households (80 per cent of the core target group) to achieve at least one of the following: (i) increase household asset ownership; (ii) increase in household savings; reduction in prevalence of child malnutrition; and (iv) reduction in food insecurity.The programme will support the efforts of the Ministry of Agriculture and Cooperatives (MACO) to:  (i) prioritize its research efforts on priority issues for smallholder farmers in northern Zambia; (ii) strengthen the linkages between agricultural extension and research; (iii) appropriately tailor its approaches for extension; (v) coordinate external donor-financed initiatives, learn from them and integrate positive features into its approach; (v) strengthen its capacity for planning, managing and delivering farmer services; and (vi) develop approaches for promoting, regulating and monitoring service provision by non-government actors.

title: Credit and Financial Services: Rural Finance Expansion Programme

This will be indicated by increases in the number (about 140,000 households) and percentage of the adult population using financial services, and a decline in the cost of borrowing.

title: Irrigation: Smallholder Irrigation Support Programme
description:
The development goal of the programme is to increase the incomes and food security of
smallholder irrigating households and households in neighbouring communities on a sustainable basis.
This will be dependent on the achievement of outputs at both sectoral and scheme levels. At the sectoral level, the programme will aim to enhance the institutional and regulatory framework for smallholder irrigation; while, at the scheme level, it will look to ensure that farmers are themselves able to manage, operate and maintain fully operational and productive irrigation schemes. As a subsectoral programme with a seven-year implementation period, SISP will assist the Government from the short-, mediumand long-term perspective. Short-term requirements will be served by, and immediate benefits
derived from, investments at the individual scheme and institutional levels. In the medium term, the
programme¿s links with the ASIP will be expected to further improve the policy and legal framework
for smallholder irrigation and the institutional capacity to efficiently serve the subsector. Over the
long term, the programme will assist the Government in developing suitable methodologies and
public/private sector partnerships for coordinated, catchment-based planning for expanded command
area development.

title: Irrigation: Smallholder Irrigation Revitalization Programme
description:
The overall goal of SIRP is that rural households achieve food and nutrition security and are resilient to climate change effects and economic shocks in the programme districts. The programme development objective is that rural households sustainably increase their income in SIRP supported schemes and adjacent rainfed areas. 
The programme goal will be achieved by revitalizing existing high potential irrigation schemes and their adjacent rainfed areas (sub-catchment areas) which will result to (i) an increase in production and productivity of selected commodities; (ii) an increase of annual household income; (iii) increased market integration; and (iv) in a smallholder agricultural production system that is better adapted to climate change.
